name: The internet — a matte wire globe on a stand
build: blender -b --factory-startup --python source/build_internet_endpoint.py, then glTF-Transform dedup → weld → meshopt
units: metres; origin at the centre of the base
lod: one level. It is the heaviest asset in the library (96 meridian/parallel segments) and it is never a hero: if a film needs many of them, build a low-poly variant.

anchors.port_in: where the provider's line arrives, at the base (outward normal -X)
anchors.centre: the centre of the globe — for a callout

why_not_hardware: The internet has no box to show. Drawn as glowing 'cyber' graphics it becomes decoration; drawn as a data centre it teaches something false about where a school's traffic goes. A matte globe in the same materials and the same light as the hardware says what it needs to: somewhere far away that answers.
behaviour: no lights. It is either reached or it is not, and the film says which with the signal, not with a state on this object.

provenance.origin: original work, authored for OE by the explainer engine (procedural Blender script)
provenance.creator: OE Support explainer engine
provenance.license: OE-owned; no third-party geometry, textures or trademarks
